acceptance_criteria.criterion: `insights.js` project links use `#/projects/{repo}/{slug}` when `repository_name` is available
`knowledge.js` origin-plan links use `#/projects/{repo}/{slug}` when `repository_name` is available
Entries with null `repository_name` do not generate broken links — graceful fallback is applied
No link in either view still uses the bare-slug form without repo

summary: Updated insights.js to generate namespaced project links (#/projects/{repo}/{slug}) when repository_name is non-null; falls back to plain text (no broken link) when null.

Updated knowledge.js to generate namespaced origin-plan links (#/projects/{repo}/{slug}) when both origin_plan and repository_name are present; falls back to a plain <span> (no anchor) when repository_name is null.
Added new test file tests/gui/insights-knowledge-links.test.ts with 9 tests covering all 4 acceptance criteria using jsdom + vm.runInThisContext (same approach as client-rendering.test.ts).
Full test suite: 93 files, 2843 tests — all passing, zero regressions.

comments.note: insights.js buildCards() constructs HTML via string concatenation throughout. A helper function like `projectHref(repo, slug)` could reduce duplication if other card elements ever need namespaced links. Not in scope for this WP but worth noting.

knowledge.js applyFilters() silently discards items whose scope doesn't match activeTab; there is no empty-state indicator for the 'repository' tab when no repository insights exist. Pre-existing issue, not introduced here.
knowledge.js uses a mix of `/* ── comment ── */` (dense divider style) and standard `//` line comments. Not a bug, but slightly inconsistent with the rest of the file suite. No change needed.

summary: Build check: no compilation errors — browser-side JS files load cleanly in jsdom via vm.runInThisContext.
AC-1 PASS: insights.js generates #/projects/{encodeURIComponent(repo)}/{encodeURIComponent(slug)} anchor when repository_name is non-null (lines 40-42).
AC-2 PASS: knowledge.js generates #/projects/{encodeURIComponent(repo)}/{encodeURIComponent(origin_plan)} anchor when both origin_plan and repository_name are non-null (lines 198-202).

AC-3 PASS: insights.js falls back to escapeHtml(project_slug) plain text when repository_name is null/undefined/empty (falsy check). knowledge.js falls back to <span> when repository_name is falsy, empty string when origin_plan is absent.
AC-4 PASS: grep of all *.js view files confirms no bare-slug #/projects/{slug} pattern in insights.js or knowledge.js — both use encodeURIComponent for both segments.
Dedicated test suite (insights-knowledge-links.test.ts): 9 tests, all PASS.
Full regression: 93 test files, 2843 tests — all PASS, zero regressions.

comments.note: insights.js falsy check on repository_name (`e.repository_name ? ...`) handles null, undefined, and empty string identically — all fall back to plain text. This is slightly broader than the spec's 'null' wording but behaves correctly and defensively for all API response shapes.

Edge case verified: undefined project_slug in insights.js fallback path renders the string 'undefined' as text via escapeHtml(e.project_slug). This is a pre-existing pattern across the entire view suite and is not introduced by this WP — API schema guarantees project_slug is always populated.

No test covers the case where project_slug itself contains special characters requiring URL encoding in the insights.js namespaced link path. The URL-encoding test does cover this for knowledge.js origin_plan. Low risk since slugs are plan directory names which are typically URL-safe.

summary: Reviewed insights.js (lines 40-42): conditional projectLink construction is correct — falsy guard on repository_name is appropriately defensive, encodeURIComponent applied to both segments, escapeHtml fallback applied consistently with surrounding HTML generation patterns.

Reviewed knowledge.js (lines 198-202): nested ternary for originPlanHtml is readable and correctly handles three cases: no origin_plan → empty string, origin_plan present but no repository_name → <span> fallback, both present → namespaced anchor. No off-by-one or logic errors.

Reviewed test file insights-knowledge-links.test.ts (9 tests): all four acceptance criteria are covered including URL-encoding of special characters, repository_name null/undefined fallbacks, bare-slug absence check, and link text content. Test structure (jsdom + vm.runInThisContext) is consistent with the established project pattern.
No blocking issues found. No Fix-Forward changes applied. One Documentation-Forward item tagged.

comments.note: insights.js lines 40-42: the falsy guard `e.repository_name ? ... : ...` is slightly broader than the spec's 'null' wording but is the correct defensive choice — it silently handles null, undefined, and empty string from any API response shape without special-casing. Pattern is consistent with the existing code style in this file.

knowledge.js lines 198-202: the nested ternary `ins.origin_plan ? (ins.repository_name ? <anchor> : <span>) : ''` is concise and readable for three cases. If a fourth branch is ever needed (e.g., global-scope origin link without a repository), extraction into a named helper `buildOriginPlanHtml(ins)` would improve readability.

[documentation-forward] Neither insights.js nor knowledge.js has inline comments explaining the namespaced link format `#/projects/{repo}/{slug}`. A one-line comment at the projectLink / originPlanHtml assignment site (e.g., `/* namespaced link: requires repository_name so the router can scope the project view */`) would help future contributors understand why the fallback exists and when it triggers.

Test: insights-knowledge-links.test.ts line 284 asserts `app.innerHTML.toContain('<span style="font-size:12px">Origin:')` — this hard-codes the inline style string. If the style is refactored to a class, this test will fail. Low risk for now but worth noting as a brittleness vector.

summary: Addressed the documentation-forward item from the code-review pipeline: added inline comments at the projectLink assignment site in insights.js (lines 40–43) and the originPlanHtml assignment site in knowledge.js (lines 198–203), explaining the namespaced link format (#/projects/{repo}/{slug}), why repository_name is required, and when the fallback path triggers.
insights.js comment explains: requires repository_name for router scoping; null repository_name falls back to plain escaped text (no anchor, no broken link).
knowledge.js comment covers all three cases: no origin_plan → empty string; origin_plan + repository_name → namespaced anchor; origin_plan without repository_name → <span> fallback.
